pull.title: KAFKA-21111 [2/N]: Grant tasks at once to members that cannot be warmed up
pull.body:
This is the second change of the series that makes the warm-up task
refiner (KAFKA-20665) compatible with clients that speak version 0 of
the streams group heartbeat (see KAFKA-21111), on top of #23761.

A warm-up task can only complete a migration if the coordinator observes
the target owner restoring it, which a member that heartbeats with
version 0 never allows, as it does not report task offsets. When the
target assignment moves a stateful task to such a member, the refiner no
longer stages the migration. It lets the target assignment through for
that task, so the current owner revokes it and the target owner takes it
over, as it would without a refiner.

The check sits after the readiness check, so that a move between two
members of one process still happens inside the instance, and before the
analysis of the incumbent and of the copies, so that a caught-up copy on
another process is not promoted as a temporary owner. That detour would
only postpone the same cold grant and add a second hand-over. The
version of the current owner is irrelevant: a member that processes a
task is hot by definition, and keeps it while a target owner that can be
warmed up restores it. If the target owner already holds a standby task
of the task, the client recycles it into the active task, so the grant
is warm in the common case, even though the coordinator cannot see that.

The refiner is not the default yet, so this change is not live. The
tests cover the grant, the missing detour through a caught-up copy, and
a current owner of version 0 that keeps its task.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>

review_comments.body:
This `@param` documents `warmupSupport`, but `analyzeTasks` has no parameter by that name. Javadoc reports unmatched parameter tags; keep only the `heartbeatVersions` entry.

This issue also appears on line 317 of the same file.

@@ -237,12 +238,19 @@ static Map indexProcessLoad( * *

Only an active-running or caught-up copy is ever promoted. * + *

A task whose target owner is {@link WarmupSupport#NOT_SUPPORTED} is never staged: its target owner never + * reports its restore progress, so no warm-up task could ever be seen to complete the migration. + * * @param currentAssignment * The indexed current assignment, from {@link #indexCurrentAssignment}. * @param targetAssignment * All members' target assignments, as computed by the task assignor. * @param members * All members of the group, used to resolve which process a member runs in. + * @param warmupSupport + * Whether each member may be handed a warm-up task. + * @param heartbeatVersions + * The version of the latest heartbeat of each member, which tells whether a member can be warmed up.
review_comments.body: Fixed in 4df855bc67. There was only one such tag in the file.

This handles only a known version-0 member, but `UNKNOWN` also cannot safely receive a new warm-up. After coordinator failover the version map is empty, so a migration to a target process with no existing copy is staged and `planWarmups` plants a warm-up, contrary to `AssignmentRefiner`'s contract and potentially stranding a version-0 target. Handle `UNKNOWN` separately: retain staging only when the target process already holds the copy; otherwise grant the task directly, and cover both paths with tests.

Unknown versions after a failover are handled in a follow-up PR of this series. It won't grant directly, though: right after a failover every member is unknown, so granting would turn every pending migration into a cold hand-over. Instead, while any member is unknown, the refiner keeps migrations staged and funds no new warm-up tasks until every member has heartbeated.
Consider adding a test where the v0 target owner already holds a standby of the task.
Added in ed325b951e. Without the grant, that standby would be borrowed and never seen to catch up, so the migration would stay staged forever.

issue.title: KAFKA-21111 [3/N]: Promote the standby of an orphan on a member that cannot report its progress

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
This is the third change of the series that makes the warm-up task
refiner (KAFKA-20665) compatible with clients that speak version 0 of
the streams group heartbeat (see KAFKA-21111), on top of #23784.

A copy of a task on a member that does not report its restore progress
can never be observed to be caught up, so it is neither promoted nor
protected, like any other copy that is not caught up. There is one
exception, for an orphan: a stateful task that nobody holds as an active
task, whose target owner can be warmed up but holds no state for it. If
the target assignment also names the holder of the unobservable copy as
a standby holder of the task, the holder runs the task as temporary
owner while the target owner warms up. A holder that heartbeats with
version 0, or whose version is not known yet, is such a member.

Here the alternative to promoting a copy of unknown lag is a restore
from scratch on the target owner next to a standby task that would have
to restore anyway, whereas elsewhere the alternative is keeping a
running owner. If the copy turns out to be stale, the temporary owner
restores it as an active task before it processes anything, which is the
restore the target assignment demands of it as a standby holder anyway.
If it is close, the task resumes processing at once. The hand-over then
demotes the temporary owner to its standby task in place.

The refiner is not the default yet, so this change is not live. The
tests cover the promotion for a holder of version 0 and for one of
unknown version, and the cases where it must not apply: a holder that
reports being behind, a standby that the target assignment does not keep
on its holder, and a target owner that cannot be warmed up.

Reviewers: Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>
